findings.F1: The break's rise keeps building well past the tested 5 days. Over the same 2,744 to 2,444 cases, the unusual move per case is +0.71 % at 5 days (t 2.55, strength 0.052), +1.33 % at 10 days (t 3.24, strength 0.070) and +2.30 % at 20 days (t 3.53, strength 0.080). The 20-day unusual move alone is about 10 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
findings.F2: Almost all of the edge sits in the strongest breaks. In the top quartile of entry forecast (679 cases), the strength is 0.139 at 5 days, 0.154 at 10 days and 0.182 at 20 days. The three lower quartiles sit between 0.007 and 0.096, with no order among them.
findings.F3: Much of the break's move happens on the signal's own bar, before a trader acting at its close can capture it. That bar's unusual return is +5.6 % (t 31.5 over 2,693 cases), against +0.71 % over the 5 days after it.
findings.F4: The break's continuation is uneven across years and coins. The 5-day unusual move is positive in 2019, 2020, 2021, 2023 and 2024 (t up to 4.0) and negative in 2018 (t -2.2), 2022 (t -3.1) and 2025 (t -1.3). Only 2 of 19 coins reach t 2 on their own (ZEC t 2.25; AVAX t 1.98 is just below).
findings.F5: There is a weekday pattern the idea does not explain. Saturday's unusual daily return is positive in both halves of the data (t 4.1 up to 2021, t 2.4 after), in both coin groups (t 4.1 on the six old coins, 2.5 on the 13 newer), and in 7 of 8 years. Thursday's is negative in both halves (t -1.3 and -3.9), in both groups (t -2.9 and -2.1), and in 6 of 8 years. The book earns most of its gain on Fridays and Saturdays (+0.22 % and +0.20 % per day, t 6.6 and 6.5), against at most 0.07 % on the other days.
findings.F6: Across all bars, nearness to the 90-day high and the 20-day return do not order the 5-day move. The top quintile of nearness has a strength of 0.073 (t 2.1), but the second-lowest has -0.109 (t -4.3) and the lowest +0.036. The 20-day return quintiles run +0.025, -0.064, -0.026, +0.007, +0.066. Neither is graded.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, after a rise over its past 20 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 20 days. The more times the level held, the further the close sits above it and the larger the 20-day rise, the larger the rise that follows.
ideas.consequence: A strong break of a repeatedly held level after a run is a reason to hold the buy for weeks rather than days, since the move is still growing at four times the tested horizon.
ideas.name: breakout continuation over weeks
